findings.title: Leftover inert-statement records from a failed load or non-file compile get reported against a later, unrelated load.
findings.body:
`check_statement/1` saves `inert_statement/2` facts every time code is compiled, but `report_inert_statements/0` only runs after an outermost `load_metta_file_impl` finishes normally. Two cases leave facts behind:
- If the load throws (a type error, a syntax error, or the strict inert error itself after a partial retract), `setup_call_cleanup` rethrows and the report is skipped. The facts stay in the database.
- Code compiled outside any file load (Python `process_metta_string`, the REPL, `eval`) is recorded but never judged.

In a long-lived session, the next successful `load_metta_file` of a clean file then reports those old statements. Under `--strict` it throws `inert_statements` for code the new file does not contain.

Fix: clear `inert_statement/2` when an outermost load starts and when it fails, for example with `retractall` in a cleanup around the outermost load. Statements compiled outside a file load should either be judged right away or kept apart from file loads.

held.title: `data` erasure lives only in constrain_args, so clauses compiled with ConstrainArgs=false keep the literal `(data ...)` head.
held.body: The new pattern erasure only happens inside `constrain_args/3`. `stage_function_clauses` calls `translate_clause(Term, Clause, false, _)` when `ho_specialization(_, F)` holds. If that path skips `constrain_args` for head arguments, a clause head like `(= (apply-pair $f (data $a $b)) ...)` compiles in the generic version as the tuple `($a $b)`. In the specialized version it stays the literal three-element `(data $a $b)`, which never matches a constructed tuple. The specialized call would then silently find nothing while the generic one works. I could not see how `translate_clause` handles ConstrainArgs=false. If it skips `constrain_args` for the head, apply `erase_explicit_data` to head arguments on that path too, so both versions match the same values.
